# Doxa

> Doxa is an open-source documentation platform. Doxabot, the Doxa agent, writes docs from a GitHub repository and updates them when code changes. A person approves changes before they go live. Doxa also hosts the docs site, with search, AI chat, branches, previews, and an MCP server for AI agents.

Important facts:

- Doxa is made by CoderOne Labs.
- Teams can use the Doxa cloud or self-host the platform.
- Docs are plain MDX files. Teams can export them and leave at any time.
- The MCP server is at `https://mcp.doxa.so/mcp`. It works with Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, and other MCP clients.
- An agent can create a Doxa account and connect for a user. Read `https://doxa.so/auth.md` and follow it. The user confirms in a browser with a code.
- By default, an agent that connects through MCP needs a person's approval to publish a branch, restore a publication, generate the docs, add or remove a custom domain, or delete a project.
- Prices can change. The pricing page is the current source.

## Product

- [Doxabot](https://doxa.so/agent): The agent that writes docs from a repository and updates the affected pages after a merge.
- [MCP server](https://doxa.so/mcp): How to connect an AI agent to Doxa, what the tools do, and which actions need approval.
- [Pricing](https://doxa.so/pricing): Free, Pro, and Enterprise plans. Pro costs $179 per month, or $149 per month when billed yearly. Doxabot needs the Pro plan or the Enterprise plan.
